gaps.explanation: fail takes the to-infinitive: failed to meet.

gaps.sentence: I resent ___ treated as an amateur when I have twenty years’ experience.
gaps.explanation: 'Resent' takes a gerund; the passive is 'being treated'.

gaps.sentence: It was kind of them ___ us a lift to the station.
gaps.explanation: 'It was kind of them to give …' — to-infinitive after the adjective.

gaps.sentence: They managed ___ the fire before it spread.
gaps.explanation: manage takes the to-infinitive: managed to put out.

gaps.sentence: The hotel offered ___ our room free of charge.
gaps.explanation: offer takes the to-infinitive: offered to upgrade.

gaps.sentence: Renovating the kitchen involved ___ a wall.
The scheme aims ___ younger visitors to the museum.
gaps.explanation: aim + to-infinitive: aims to attract (aim at + -ing is also possible in BrE).

gaps.sentence: I look forward to ___ your suggestions at the meeting.
